goal: Plan AWG V1.9 maintenance inbox and reconciliation

body:
## Purpose
V1.9 should make AWG actively resist graph decay. By this point AWG can store rich knowledge, attribute writes to runs, render human-friendly node details, and understand related vault topology. The next highest-value slice is an agent-facing maintenance inbox and append-only reconciliation model so agents can see what needs attention before stale, duplicated, unsupported, or unresolved knowledge becomes invisible.

## Primary Outcome
An agent can run a deterministic inbox command and immediately see the highest-priority maintenance work: stale knowledge, duplicate-ish nodes, orphans, evidence gaps, open questions, active risks/blockers, proposed decisions that may be stale, and cross-vault topology issues. The same data should feed doctor, run preflight, handoff, task lens, and the viewer without adding a daemon, database, network service, or AI dependency.

## Non-Goals
Do not add semantic/vector search, hosted sync, a daemon, MCP, plugin execution, multi-user permissions, arbitrary merge rewriting, or destructive cleanup. V1.9 should not try to solve full role/domain lenses, arbitrary dashboards, claims/evidence verification, or concurrent multi-agent locking. It should build the reliable maintenance substrate those later slices need.

## Definition Of Done
AWG can deterministically say what needs maintenance, why it matters, how severe it is, which nodes/runs/vault relationships are involved, and which conservative commands could repair or review the issue. Reconciliation is append-only: agents can mark duplicates, supersession, contradictions, canonical relationships, and resolutions without deleting or rewriting canonical history.
summary: Build deterministic maintenance queues and append-only reconciliation so agents can keep AWG brains fresh, de-duplicated, evidenced, and reviewable over time.
title: AWG V1.9: maintenance inbox and reconciliation

body:
## Required Queues
V1.9 should derive a maintenance inbox from compiled graph state, diagnostics, run attribution, freshness metadata, evidence links, and topology indexes. Initial queue kinds should include: stale, needs_review, duplicates, orphans, evidence, questions, risks, blockers, decisions, topology, and hygiene.

## Prioritization
Each item should have deterministic severity and priority. Suggested severity values: info, warning, error. Suggested priority inputs: fatal diagnostics first, completed work missing evidence, active blockers/risks, stale high-importance nodes, duplicate candidates, orphan nodes, unanswered questions, topology warnings, and lower-risk hygiene items.

## Agent Use
The inbox should be small and actionable by default. Agents need item IDs, codes, reasons, involved node IDs/run IDs/vault IDs, suggested commands, and whether the item is safe for autonomous repair or needs human review.
summary: Derive prioritized maintenance queues for stale, duplicate, orphaned, unsupported, unresolved, risky, and topology-related graph issues.
title: V1.9 requirement: deterministic maintenance inbox queues

body:
## Inbox Item Shape
Suggested JSON shape:

```json
{
  "id": "mi:...",
  "kind": "stale|duplicates|orphans|evidence|questions|risks|blockers|decisions|topology|hygiene",
  "code": "AWG_INBOX_STALE_NODE",
  "severity": "info|warning|error",
  "priority": 80,
  "message": "Node is past review_after and still marked current.",
  "nodeIds": ["n:..."],
  "edgeIds": [],
  "runIds": [],
  "vaultIds": [],
  "relationshipIds": [],
  "reasons": ["review_after is in the past"],
  "suggestedCommands": ["awg update node n:... --status needs_review"],
  "autonomousSafe": true,
  "needsHumanReview": false
}
```

IDs should be deterministic from kind/code/targets so repeated builds are stable. Unknown fields should be preserved where events are involved, but compiled inbox items can be derived objects.
summary: Define stable, deterministic JSON for maintenance inbox items so agents can parse and act on graph hygiene work.
title: V1.9 contract: maintenance inbox item JSON

body:
## Reconciliation Principle
V1.9 should not destructively merge or delete graph history. Reconciliation should be represented as durable append-only graph events or nodes/edges that compile into clear current-state relationships.

## Initial Relationships
Support or document these reconciliation relations: duplicate_of, canonical_for, supersedes, superseded_by, contradicts, resolved_by, verified_by, derived_from, and intentionally_open.

## Commands
Recommended CLI surface:
- `awg reconcile duplicate <a> <b> --canonical <id> [--reason "..."] [--json]`
- `awg reconcile supersede <old> <new> [--reason "..."] [--json]`
- `awg reconcile contradict <a> <b> [--reason "..."] [--json]`
- `awg reconcile resolved-by <target> <resolver> [--reason "..."] [--json]`

These commands should append normal events/edges, preserve run attribution, and never mutate old log entries. They should fail clearly for missing targets and avoid cross-vault writes unless an explicit future topology contract allows it.
summary: Represent duplicates, supersession, contradictions, canonical relationships, and resolutions as append-only graph history, not destructive merges.
title: V1.9 contract: append-only reconciliation model

body:
## Commands
Add or improve:
- `awg inbox [--kind <kind>] [--limit <n>] [--json]`
- `awg inbox show <item-id> [--json]` if useful
- `awg reconcile ...` commands for append-only cleanup markers
- `awg doctor --fix-suggestions --json` should share suggestion generation with the inbox where practical

## Integrations
Inbox data should feed: doctor, run finish preflight, handoff, task lens, resume lens if budget allows, and the viewer maintenance surface. Handoff should mention high-priority unresolved inbox items. Run preflight should include inbox items affecting touched nodes. Task lens should include inbox items related to the goal or matching nodes.

## Viewer
Add a minimal read-only maintenance route if it fits the existing viewer architecture: queue filters, item detail, linked nodes, suggested commands, and severity. Do not redesign the viewer.
summary: Expose maintenance inbox and reconciliation through stable CLI/JSON, doctor/preflight/handoff/lens integrations, and a small viewer surface if low-risk.
title: V1.9 contract: inbox CLI and integration surfaces

body:
## Main Risks
- Inbox bloat: too many low-value items makes agents ignore it.
- False duplicate candidates: simple lexical matching can overstate duplicates.
- Unsafe repair suggestions: agents may run commands that mutate too much.
- Reconciliation ambiguity: duplicate/supersede/contradict semantics can become unclear.
- Cross-vault leakage: topology inbox items must not read private/full data beyond the relationship visibility contract.
- Preflight friction: completed runs should be warned strongly, but partial/blocked/failed runs must remain usable.

## Mitigations
Keep defaults compact, deterministic, and conservative. Mark candidate duplicates as review items rather than facts. Suggestions should prefer review/status/evidence/link commands, never destructive commands. Keep reconciliation relations documented and narrow. Keep cross-vault inbox items summary-only unless the relationship explicitly allows more. Add tests for JSON stability and non-mutating dry/read paths.
summary: Maintenance inbox and reconciliation can fail through bloat, false duplicates, unsafe suggestions, ambiguous semantics, cross-vault leakage, or excessive preflight friction.
title: V1.9 risk register: maintenance inbox and reconciliation

body:
## Required Test Areas
- Inbox derivation for stale nodes, needs_review nodes, orphans, evidence gaps, unanswered questions, active risks/blockers, proposed decisions, duplicate candidates, doctor diagnostics, and topology issues.
- Stable JSON item shape with deterministic IDs, severity, priority, target IDs, suggested commands, and autonomous/human review flags.
- `awg inbox --json`, kind filtering, limits, empty vault behavior, and parseable output.
- Reconciliation commands append events/edges with run attribution, preserve unknown fields, fail clearly for missing targets, and do not mutate old events.
- Doctor fix suggestions and inbox suggestions stay aligned and non-mutating.
- Run finish preflight includes relevant inbox items for touched nodes without blocking partial/blocked/failed runs too aggressively.
- Handoff and task lens include compact unresolved maintenance context within budget.
- Viewer maintenance route does not crash on missing/old inbox data.
- Old vaults without reconciliation events still compile.
- Tests isolate HOME/temp dirs and do not touch real ~/.awg.
summary: Test derived inbox queues, stable JSON, reconciliation commands, doctor/preflight/handoff/lens integrations, viewer compatibility, and old-vault behavior.
title: V1.9 test plan: maintenance inbox and reconciliation

body:
## Suggested Slices
1. Inspect current diagnostics, preflight, handoff, task lens, freshness, duplicate-ish diagnostics, topology diagnostics, and viewer data generation.
2. Create a core maintenance inbox derivation module that consumes compiled graph state and emits stable inbox items.
3. Add `awg inbox` CLI with `--json`, `--kind`, and budget/limit behavior.
4. Share conservative suggestion helpers between inbox and doctor where practical.
5. Add append-only reconciliation commands and compiler interpretation of reconciliation relations.
6. Integrate relevant inbox items into run preflight, handoff, task lens, and resume/current view if low-risk.
7. Add a minimal read-only viewer maintenance route if it fits without redesign.
8. Update docs, generated instructions, examples, and tests.
9. Run adversarial/peer review loops after each meaningful slice: 1 reviewer for low-risk docs or CLI polish, 2 reviewers for core inbox/reconciliation logic, and 3 reviewers only for final release readiness or cross-cutting behavior.
summary: Implement V1.9 in slices: derive inbox items, expose CLI, share suggestions, add reconciliation, integrate surfaces, update viewer/docs/tests, and use bounded reviewer loops.
title: V1.9 implementation sequence and review loop

body:
The user priority after V1.9 is: V2.0 view primitives / human operating surfaces, V2.2 claims-evidence-verification, V2.3 agent work queues, and V2.4 multi-agent coordination. Role/domain lenses remain useful but should not become a fixed hard-coded domain pack release. When AWG revisits lenses, agents should be encouraged to define, review, and iterate vault-local lens configurations similar to operating templates, so lenses adapt to the actual domain and project rather than forcing universal categories.

This means V1.9 should avoid overfitting to role lenses. It should expose generic maintenance inbox data and stable primitives that future configurable lenses can consume.
summary: After V1.9, prioritize view primitives, claims/evidence verification, work queues, and multi-agent coordination; defer role/domain lenses until they can be vault-configured by agents like templates.
title: Roadmap decision: prioritize maintenance substrate before configurable lenses
